textual.context: Presented as a first-person tutorial or demonstration; the surrounding wording for the token-doubling reference is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: The described token-submission action is paired with an apparent token-doubling return reference, creating a reward/action relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The closing ASR phrase is garbled; these records do not establish that token doubling is a promise, that viewers are directed to act, or that any transfer or outcome occurred.

visual.observation: A platform interface shows an option to submit 10,000 tokens for mining at a displayed difficulty of 20.0000; its transaction history shows an outgoing 10,000 entry labeled "Submit 10000 tokens on difficulty 20.0000" alongside two incoming 5,000 entries labeled "Split bonus."
visual.context: The material appears to be a screen recording or demonstration of an account dashboard and mining interface; no explicit promotional, warning, reporting, or parody context is visible in the sampled frames.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible submission action and difficulty condition are directly associated in the displayed transaction history with incoming entries labeled "Split bonus," presenting a token-return relationship that may merit review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames cannot establish whether the displayed balances or transactions are genuine, whether any transfer occurred outside the interface, or whether the bonus was actually received or withdrawable.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker says the post-refresh display is inaccurate while the system updates and says not to worry about changes not appearing immediately.

evidence.quote: Once the page refreshes you'll see this, but this is not accurate.
The system now needs to update.
Don't worry if you don't see the changes immediately.

visual_context_notes.observation: The mining interface visibly states "YOU ARE NOT MINING" while also displaying token-submission controls and mining-related account information.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it actively promotes a OneCoin token-mining process and instructs viewers to submit their tokens through the platform's Exchange and Mining menus. It presents submitting 10,000 tokens and receiving a split bonus or token doubling as the intended benefit, rather than reporting, criticizing, or testing the scheme. The video therefore solicits participation involving a consequential transfer of tokens within the promoted system.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S04 is the best-supported subtype because the content directly instructs token submission for mining, and the displayed transaction history links a token submission to entries labeled Split bonus. The supplied evidence does not explicitly establish that a mining package, hashpower, equipment share, membership or node was purchased, so the fit is limited to the observed mining-return mechanism.
